I am the Slayton Assistant Professor of East Asian Politics in the Department of Politics and Philosophy at the University of Idaho. I study domestic politics of international relations, with China as a special empirical focus. Beyond the China case, my research seeks to understand the role of leaders and domestic institutions in shaping foreign policies and international security. My co-authored book, *Zero Tolerance: Repression and Political Violence on China's New Silk Road* (Cambridge University Press, 2022), examines how competing priorities at home and abroad shape China's domestic and foreign policies toward political violence. My other works have been published or forthcoming in *British Journal of Political Science*, *International Studies Quarterly*, and *Journal of Politics*.

Prior to UI, I was an [America in the World Consortium (AWC)](https://www.awconsortium.org/alumni/) Postdoctoral Fellow in the Department of Political Science at Duke University. I was also a Predoctoral Visiting Scholar in the [Institute for Security and Conflict Studies (ISCS)](https://iscs.elliott.gwu.edu/our-visiting-scholars) at George Washington University's Elliott School of International Affairs, and a Research Fellow affiliated with the [National Security Policy Center (NSPC)](https://nspcbatten.org/about/) of the Frank Batten School of Leadership and Public Policy at UVa. I received Ph.D. in Foreign Affairs from the Department of Politics at the University of Virginia.
